clue.text: He drew out clues to lure a criminal

definitions.note: a man who drew pictures, a painter and draughtsman

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the fifteen letters of the fodder are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective drafts misleading clues to entice a crook into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He drew' looks like a raffle or a tied match, but it means an artist. The fodder runs from 'out' to 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was the French artist famous for his posters and drawings of Montmartre nightlife.

clue.text: Coxed pair booked?

parts.note: a coxed pair is a rowing crew of two oarsmen plus a cox, so three people in a boat; 'booked' says this is the title of a book, Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel

explanation.surface: A two-person rowing crew with a cox has reserved a slot on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A coxed pair is two rowers and a coxswain: three men in one boat. 'Booked' turns that literal description into the title of Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic novel about a boating holiday on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Victorian comic novel describes three friends rowing up the Thames, much like a coxed pair's crew.

clue.text: Gave birth — all but first raised

indicators.note: everything except the opening letter is kept, so the leading letter of the word for giving birth is dropped

parts.note: a bitch that gave birth pupped, producing a litter of puppies

explanation.surface: A family announcement about a birth, oddly followed by something being lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To up a price or offer is to increase it, so upped is a synonym for raised or increased.

clue.text: Bulb obscuring private eye's view

indicators.note: the bulb covers and so hides the detective, placing his letters inside its own

parts.note: an onion is a bulb, the vegetable grown from one
a private eye is a PI, a private investigator; the 's is a link meaning 'is' or 'has'

explanation.surface: A light bulb blocks a detective's line of sight during a stakeout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a lamp, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of a personal belief or judgement is an opinion, as in 'in my view'.

clue.text: Weavers briefly disperse in disarray

indicators.note: letters in disarray are muddled and out of order, so the shortened fodder is rearranged
a word cut short loses its last letter, so the final E of the fodder goes

explanation.surface: A crowd of weaving workers quickly breaks up and scatters in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims DISPERSE to DISPERS, and 'in disarray' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders spin and weave webs, so they are weavers in the animal world.

clue.text: Liberal leader in news that is breaking fast

indicators.note: the other pieces break into the fast, splitting its letters apart

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of 'news'

parts.note: i.e., id est, is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A political report about the Liberal Party's leader in a breaking news story about a hunger strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal leader' looks like a phrase giving one letter, but 'Liberal' is the definition and 'leader' belongs to 'news'. The Christian fast is split in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of tolerant and not strict is a synonym for lenient, as of a forgiving judge.

clue.text: Free credit granted to global union?

parts.note: the global union is the UN, the United Nations; something granted to it is the UN's
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: An organisation offering free loans to the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Credit given to the UN would be 'the UN's tick'; 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstick something stuck is to release or free it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ran through and staggered out

parts.note: to reel is to stagger unsteadily, so staggered gives reeled
off and out both mean away, as in a light being out or off

explanation.surface: A drunk ran down the street and stumbled out of the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran through' looks like a description of running, but it means recited quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off a list is to recite it quickly and fluently, just as one runs through it.

clue.text: Helped EEC cut horsemeat supply

indicators.note: read as an adverb, supply means in a supple, flexible way, so the fodder letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A news story about the European Economic Community cutting supplies of horsemeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun about trade, but it is read as 'supplely', bending the fifteen letters from EEC to horsemeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to the rescue is to step in and help someone in difficulty, an idiom for assisting.

clue.text: Loathsome agent returning to fix it

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is an agent for a company

indicators.note: coming back means the phrase for fixing it is read backwards

parts.note: to nail it is to fix it firmly in place

explanation.surface: A despicable spy comes back to repair something.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptilian, like a cold-blooded snake, is used figuratively for someone repellent, creepy or contemptible.

clue.text: Cook finally serves crew

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word serves, its last letter

parts.note: a crew of workers is a team

explanation.surface: In a kitchen, the chef at last serves the staff their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the chef in the scene, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is a method of cooking food over boiling water, so to steam is to cook.

clue.text: Upright sage pursuing objective

indicators.note: one piece chasing another comes after it, so the wise word follows the objective

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective
a sage is wise, an adjective for someone knowing

explanation.surface: An honest wise man chasing his goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Endwise means with the end upwards, standing on end, hence upright.

clue.text: Nutmeg's got over depression, that's clear

indicators.note: turned over means the setter's 'I have' is flipped round and read backwards

parts.note: Nutmeg is the setter, so Nutmeg has got means I've got, giving I'VE
a dent is a small depression in a surface

explanation.surface: The setter has recovered from low spirits, and that much is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got over depression' reads as recovery, but 'over' reverses I'VE and the depression is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plainly visible or obvious, a direct synonym of clear.

clue.text: Last of our media men dispersed

indicators.note: taking the last of each word gives the final letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: The remaining journalists of our newspaper scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' applies to each of 'our', 'media' and 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours that ran in the wash spread and dispersed through the fabric.

clue.text: Old vessel, extremely dangerous, blows up

parts.note: ex- means former or old, as in ex-wife
a pan is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of dangerous

explanation.surface: An ancient ship packed with something very hazardous explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows up' suggests an explosion, but it means grows larger, as with a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a balloon or a photograph is to make it bigger, which is what something does when it expands.

clue.text: Favourite uncle hurt about aunt's initial pique

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite

indicators.note: the rearranged uncle goes about, around, the aunt's first letter
hurt in the sense of damaged, so the letters of uncle are knocked out of order
the initial of a word is its first letter, here the start of aunt's

explanation.surface: A favourite uncle offended by something his aunt says, causing a family huff.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a fit of irritation from wounded pride, which is petulance, sulky bad temper.

clue.text: Expected sound of early precipitation

indicators.note: sound of tells us to say the word aloud and enter one spelt differently

parts.note: dew is moisture that condenses overnight and is seen in the early morning

explanation.surface: A weather forecast predicting the noise of an early shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A train that is due is expected to arrive at a scheduled time, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Remove date

definitions.meaning: to take something out is to remove or extract it
to take someone out is to go on a date with them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two senses: extracting something, and escorting someone for a romantic evening.

clue.text: Girl close to granny's heart

indicators.note: close to means near the heart, rather than at its exact centre, so letters next to the middle are taken
the heart of a word is its central part, here the core of granny's

explanation.surface: A young girl who is dear to her grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a common girl's name, so a crossword can define it as a girl.

clue.text: Number, say, coming or going in Bury

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say can go in either way round, forwards or backwards, and still give the same result

parts.note: to inter someone is to bury them
e.g., exempli gratia, means 'for example' or 'say'

explanation.surface: A Bury football fan's chant about a number of people arriving and leaving the town.
explanation.walkthrough: EG inside INT_ER and GE inside INTE_R both give the answer, hence 'coming or going'. Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, so a specific kind of number.

clue.text: Info about youth meeting daughter, please

indicators.note: the information goes around the young man and daughter, holding them inside

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: meeting means joining up with, so the daughter comes right next to the youth

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: Information about a young man meeting someone's daughter, please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a polite add-on, but it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gladden someone is to make them happy, a synonym of please or delight.

clue.text: Dish in Olympic venue's very dry

indicators.note: the dish is in the venue's letters, which hold the very-dry pieces inside

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics; the 's means 'has', so the venue holds the next words
so means very, as in so tired
TT, teetotal, describes someone who doesn't drink alcohol, so dry

explanation.surface: A meal at the Olympic host city's venue is very dry.
explanation.walkthrough: RIO's holds SO TT, giving RI-SOTT-O.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Horse bit fairy lovers on the way back

indicators.note: travelling back means the combined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: an elf is a fairy creature
fans are lovers or devotees of something

explanation.surface: A horse nips at a fairy's admirers on their journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse bit' reads as a horse biting, but it is a noun, the bit in a horse's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle is a simple jointed bit placed in a horse's mouth, attached to the reins.

clue.text: Fixed clothing US agents cut up

indicators.note: clothing means dressing, so the set covers the agents, holding them inside

parts.note: something set is fixed or firm
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: A tailor's alterations on the uniforms of FBI agents were fixed after being torn up.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment something is to divide it into sections, so to cut it up.

clue.text: Unpromising poetry of the last 2000 years

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the years since the birth of Christ, roughly the last two millennia
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses all modern poetry since ancient times as unpromising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poetry of AD' is AD verse, with AD written first.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are unfavourable or hostile, so the outlook they give is unpromising.

clue.text: Dessert on this is ready and waiting

definitions.meaning: a frozen dessert such as a sorbet

definitions.text: on this is ready and waiting
definitions.meaning: held in reserve, ready for later use

explanation.surface: A pudding sitting out, ready and waiting to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice is a frozen sweet course, and the idiom 'on ice' means kept ready and in reserve.

clue.text: Eager to gather complete cereal crop?

parts.note: all means complete, the whole
ears are the grain-bearing heads of cereal plants such as wheat

explanation.surface: A farmer keen to bring in an entire harvest of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' suggests harvesting, but here it means gather information by listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone all ears is listening intently, eager to learn or take in news.

clue.text: Was benefactor hosting immoderate dance?

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the giver's word holds the immoderate one within it

parts.note: a benefactor gives, so was a benefactor means gave
OTT, over the top, means excessive or immoderate

explanation.surface: A generous patron throws a lavish, over-the-top ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is a French dance of the 18th century, popular at court.

clue.text: Just under half an ice cream for musicians, collectively

indicators.note: keeping just under half the letters means only the opening five of the eleven letters remain

parts.note: ...-frutti is ice cream with mixed candied fruits

explanation.surface: An ice cream for a band to share.
explanation.walkthrough: The ice cream's name has eleven letters, so its opening five are just under half.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti, Italian for all, is a musical direction meaning the whole orchestra plays together.

clue.text: Admitted wearing dress, topless

indicators.note: topless means its top, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: someone wearing a gown is gowned

explanation.surface: A confession about wearing a dress with no top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' looks like a fashion detail, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to confess it, so owned is a synonym of admitted.

clue.text: Region's temperature and ice chart changing

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: changing letters around, so the words ice chart are rearranged

explanation.surface: A polar area's temperature and ice map are changing with the climate.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar zone around the North Pole is a region of the Earth.

clue.text: Family's last member is the limit!

definitions.meaning: the final descendant of a family's lineage, after whom it dies out
the phrase means the point beyond which no more can be taken, as when patience runs out

explanation.definitionFit: A family line ends with its last member, and the idiom also means a final point of tolerance.
